title: Slow Cooker White Bean & Carrot Stew
description: White beans, carrots, potatoes, and tomatoes simmer into a cheap hands-off stew made from ordinary pantry ingredients.
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use sweet potato instead of regular potato.
Stir in a handful of spinach at the end if you have it.

steps.text: Add everything to the slow cooker.
Cook until the vegetables are tender.

cookSteps.text: Add 2 cans white beans, 3 sliced carrots, 2 diced potatoes, 1 can diced tomatoes with juices, 3 cups broth, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6 hours, until the carrots and potatoes are tender.
Stir well, taste, and serve. Mash a few beans against the side of the cooker if you want a thicker broth.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months.

title: Sheet-Pan Cabbage, Potato & Egg Bowls
description: Roasted cabbage and potatoes become a filling inexpensive meal with simple eggs added at the end.
substitutions: Use sweet potato instead of regular potato.
Top with shredded cheese if desired.
Use leftover cooked potatoes and shorten roasting time.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 4 cups chopped cabbage and 1 pound diced potatoes with 1 tablespoon oil, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper on a large sheet pan.
Roast for 25–30 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the potatoes are tender and the cabbage edges are browned.
During the final 5 minutes, cook 4 eggs in a small skillet to your liking. Divide the roasted vegetables among 4 bowls and top each with an egg.

storage: Refrigerate roasted vegetables up to 4 days. Cook fresh eggs when serving if possible.

title: Leftover Pasta & White Bean Soup
description: A fast tomato-and-bean soup gives leftover cooked pasta a completely different second meal.
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use crushed tomatoes instead of diced.
Add frozen spinach or peas if you have them.

steps.text: Simmer the beans, tomatoes, broth, and seasoning.
Add leftover pasta and heat through.

cookSteps.text: Combine 1 can white beans, 1 can diced tomatoes with juices, 3 cups broth, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in a medium saucepan.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in 2 cups leftover cooked pasta and simmer 3–5 minutes, just until the pasta is hot. Top with 1/4 cup Parmesan if using.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. The pasta will soften as it sits; add broth when reheating if needed.

title: Small-Batch Peanut Butter Oat Cookies
description: A tiny batch of soft peanut-butter oat cookies uses everyday pantry ingredients and makes just enough for a small household.
substitutions: Use white sugar instead of brown sugar.
Stir in 2 tablespoons raisins or chocolate chips if desired.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Stir 1/2 cup peanut butter, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 egg, 1/2 cup oats, and 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon if using until evenly combined.
Divide into 6 mounds on a baking sheet and flatten each gently with a fork.
Bake for 10–12 minutes, until the edges look set. Cool on the pan for 5 minutes before moving them.

storage: Keep covered at room temperature up to 3 days or freeze up to 2 months.
